THE THREE-LANGUAGE DISAGREEMENT THIS ROW RECORDED IS CLOSED (phase-417 W4.e, 2026-09-18): it read "C ships `is_triggered` + `clear`, C++ ships neither, and Rust's `GuardCondition` ships only `trigger`; a polling C++ or Rust user cannot do what a polling C user can." All three ship both now -- `GuardCondition::{is_triggered,clear}` in Rust, `nros::GuardCondition::{is_triggered,clear}` over `nros_cpp_guard_condition_{is_triggered,clear}` in C++. Closing it was forced rather than optional: C's readers read the LOCAL byte in `rcl_guard_condition_t`, which only the unregistered fallback path ever wrote, so once creation became registration they would have answered `false` for every guard condition that exists -- a reader that compiles, runs and is always wrong. All three read the ARENA flag, the one `trigger` writes. BOUNDED, and the bound is part of the API: the executor CONSUMES the flag when it dispatches, so the reader answers "set and not yet dispatched"; poll it or take the callback, not both.
